title: kv-cache: refactor eviction priority + adaptive spillover/paging to reduce fragmentation and tail latency
author: Marina Chen
description: Summary: This PR refactors the KV cache eviction subsystem to address memory fragmentation, reduce host spillover frequency, and minimize tail latency during bursty workloads. Motivations: production incidents showed that large numbers of small KV entries and uneven allocation patterns caused fragmentation in GPU-resident KV arenas, triggering frequent paging/spillover to host memory and large tail-latency outliers. The old LRU-like eviction did not account for fragmentation or batching behavior, so we saw degraded throughput under continuous-batching scenarios. Changes: 1) Introduces a new eviction priority queue that scores entries by (last_access, size, fragmentation_risk, batch_hotness). This lets eviction prefer large, high-fragmentation-risk slots and retain small hot entries used by continuous batching. 2) Adds an async compaction pass that coalesces free segments within GPU arenas when fragmentation exceeds a threshold; compaction runs opportunistically and is throttled by GPU load. 3) Adaptive spillover/paging thresholds: thresholds now consider active batch depth, recent spill frequency, and configured SLOs; when batch depth is high the system raises the barrier for spillover to prioritize latency. 4) Scheduler integration: eviction/compaction decisions expose lightweight signals to the serving scheduler so it can stagger inflight requests that would otherwise increase memory pressure. 5) Kernel-level hints: the runtime now annotates KV entries with a compact metadata word to reduce CPU/GPU roundtrips during score computation. 6) Observability: new metrics (kv_eviction_score_histogram, kv_compaction_runs, kv_spillover_events, kv_fragmentation_ratio) and a /debug/kv_cache endpoint for snapshotting arena state. 7) Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for fragmentation scenarios, integration tests for continuous batching workloads, and long-running soak tests. Backcompat and safety: defaults preserve previous behavior (compat flag kv_eviction_v2=false). The adaptive modes are behind a feature flag enabled for staging by default and rollout is gated by perf/regression checks. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear ticket linked (ENG-2719) - [x] Unit tests for eviction scoring and compaction - [x] Integration tests with continuous-batching harness - [x] Perf bench results attached and compared to baseline - [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated - [x] Feature-flag guarded and staged rollout plan Notes: See design RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2719/kv-cache-eviction-refactor and incident timeline reference in ENG-2750. This description includes the implementation details, rationale, and rollout steps for reviewers to evaluate tradeoffs.
commits: Refactor eviction: add EvictionPriorityQueue, score calculation and unit tests
Add GPU arena compaction pass and throttling hooks
Expose eviction signals to scheduler and add scheduler gating logic
Add feature flag and rollout gating, update config schema
Integration tests and perf harness scenario for fragmentation workloads
Fix: reduce lock contention in eviction path (use sharded locks)
Docs: debug endpoint and observability README updates
release_notes: Improved KV cache eviction and adaptive spillover/paging to reduce fragmentation and tail latency. Adds compaction, eviction scoring, scheduler integration, and observability. Rollout guarded by feature flag (kv_eviction_v2).
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Can you quantify the perf impact? Need p90/p99 for gen throughput under the fragmentation workload compared to main.
Marina Chen: Added perf table in PR description and attached artifacts. p50 throughput unchanged, p95 improved ~12%, p99 latency reduced 28% in synthetic fragmentation scenario (see artifacts).
Priya Nair: Concern about compaction causing scheduling jitter. How is compaction throttled?

Marina Chen: Compaction is opportunistic and uses GPU load signals. It yields if GPU busy > 70% and is limited to one arena compaction per worker at a time. Added integration test to validate no increased tail latency.
Diego Morales: Suggest using sharded locks to reduce contention on hot paths (comment inline).
Marina Chen: Implemented sharded locks for eviction queue and updated unit tests.
merge_details: Merged by Liam O'Connor using squash-merge after approvals from reviewers and green CI. Rollout plan: enable kv_eviction_v2=true in staging for 48h, monitor kv_spillover_events and p99 latency before progressive rollout to production.
notes: This PR was validated on c5 and p4d-like clusters. Observed spillover events decreased by ~60% for synthetic heavy-fragmentation workloads. Watch-listed metrics: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spillover_events, kv_compaction_runs, serving_p99_latency.
